geographyNote: Township of Langley (district municipality, census subdivision), not the City of Langley

facts.text: More than 7,300 companies operate within the Township of Langley, which has a goal of one job for every resident in the employed labour force.
The Fraser Highway Employment Lands, a corridor between 228 Street and 240 Street, comprise about 500 acres outside the Agricultural Land Reserve set aside to expand industrial land supply.
Willoughby has emerged as one of the Lower Mainland's busiest development hubs, with nearly 6,700 homes submitted as development applications amid a condo and townhome construction boom.
Over the past 35 years Willoughby has grown from around 3% of the Township's population to 30%, and Council is updating the Willoughby Community Plan for completion in early 2026.

overview: The Township of Langley counted 132,603 residents in the 2021 Census, up 13.1 per cent from 2016, which is well ahead of the provincial pace. Households reported a median total income of $108,000 in 2020 and a median age of 40.8, so the customer base is largely families with buying power spread across 46,928 occupied dwellings.

That population sits on 307.22 square kilometres, so demand is split between distinct communities such as Willoughby, Walnut Grove, Fort Langley and Aldergrove. With more than 7,300 companies already operating, a local business needs to stand out neighbourhood by neighbourhood rather than rely on a single town centre.

byService.lead-generation: Because Langley added 13.1 per cent more residents between 2016 and 2021, lead generation should target newcomers in Willoughby who have not yet chosen their local suppliers.
byService.seo: Search campaigns in the Township work best when pages are built for each community, since 132,603 people live across 307.22 square kilometres and search with neighbourhood names.
byService.website-development: A website serving households with a median 2020 income of $108,000 should present clear pricing, booking and directions, since customers here can compare more than 7,300 local companies.
byService.branding: With a median age of 40.8 and a fast-growing family population, branding in Langley should feel established and dependable while still speaking to newly arrived residents.
